Hi.

I've tried to research what is involved when doing a PhD in the states but I can't really find one central place to answer all my questions. I know there is a required entrance exam that takes up the bulk of your application, the GRE, which takes a while to study for. I've heard it takes a few years longer than in Europe but it's because you take additional classes and get some teaching experience.

Are there any other differences I should be made aware of? I don't really know any of the universities in America apart from the massive ones that I probably have very little chance of getting into, so where could I go to see where some of the good ones are? What is funding like over there and how likely is it for a foreinger like myself to avail of it?

If you have any answers to these or just general comments/information I would be very grateful!
Any suggestions for a European (Irish) person considering doing a PhD in America?

Though you did not ask, I feel I should chime in on behalf of Canada. If you go to either McGill, UBC or the University of Toronto you will get a very strong education and a PhD which can take you anywhere. Admittance will usually be to a 2 year MSc, or possibly directly to a PhD program if you have a very strong application (similar to America, but a MSc in Canada is generally regarded as a valuable degree and I hear this is generally not the case in America). If your MSc goes well you will almost always have the opportunity to continue on and do a PhD, which takes 4 years. As long as you do not exceed 2 years for your MSc and 4 for your PhD, you will get full funding upon admission to the program.

There are many smaller universities in Canada where you can apply to the graduate program as well, if you are worried your application is not strong enough for the big 3 listed above. At the smaller schools you are usually fully funded as well. It is quite common for international students to do an MSc at a smaller school and then apply to a stronger school for their PhD.

Thanks for your reply. I am about to undertake an MSc here in Ireland and I'm wondering how much of an effect would that have on things. Since I wouldn't have an MSc from a Canadian universitiy, it might be harder to determine how good/bad I am with a different degree from a different country without any standardised tests. My fear is that they might decline me rather than take me on just in case I have covered different material. Do you know anything about people coming from abroad with an MSc and applying for just the PhD program? Might I have to do a one year MSc or something? Thanks again.

Your MSc will be regarded differently depending on the university you apply to, although coming from Ireland it probably counts for a lot--possibly it's regarded as having an MSc from Canada, and you could go directly to the PhD program. If you are seriously considering applying to any PhD program in Canada, this is exactly the type of question that the graduate advisor in the math department would be happy to answer.
